chores.note: What each chore costs and trains, read by the actions system (game/farm/systems/actions.gd, farm-actions spec). base = the cost before skills, tools, the season and buffs (a number, or the path of a number written elsewhere); cat = the energy category (rules/10-farming.json gather, field, ...); mult = a second modifier (a chore may switch it off for some calls in code: planting an orchard tree) that multiplies the energy after the rest (optional; the old snow and weed code did this, kept so no number moves), raw = the energy is the written number and nothing changes it (optional; the party and the visit), wear = the polish that wears, practice = the skill family that trains (both optional). A chore that works on a stretch of patch (weed, stones) or on a number of animals names its amount in code: the base energy is per unit. Other cost kinds that depend on the call (the water of a planting, the feed of the animals) come from code too. The effect of a chore stays in the system that owns it. The progression explorer reads water.fetchEnergy, which is why fetch_water points to it.
